output.title: What contact decay hides in a small business
output.body:
Contact decay is not usually a strategy problem. In a 1-10 person business, it is the quiet moment when a lead, customer, or supplier contact goes stale and nobody notices until the opportunity has already moved on. That can happen in a CRM, an inbox, or a spreadsheet that looks tidy but depends on memory to do the follow-up.

What it hides is the real workflow gap. If you do not know which contacts have gone quiet, you do not know whether the issue is lead handling, customer follow-up, or a simple lack of visibility. Human memory is a brave little filing system, but it is not a system.

The practical next step is manual: take one week of your contact list and mark every record you know has gone dormant. Then note how you noticed each one. Was it a missed reply, an old quote, a customer who never came back, or a note you found too late?

That gives you a clean decision boundary. If your contacts already live in digital tools and the quiet ones are easy to spot once you look, a lightweight flag inside your existing workflow may be worth building. If most contacts arrive by phone or walk-in, AI may not be the right fit. Once you can see which contacts have gone quiet, you will know whether the problem is worth automating.
